messages:
kai: FYI rolling a targeted canary for llm-route-mux in the 03:30 UTC change window. Plan: open flag fastfail_route to 0.2% (smoke) for 10m, then 4% for 20m, then 20% if all gates clear. We'll pin model to v3.2-rt for canary. Includes kernel micropatch and fallback-weight tweak. @nina please add to release notes.

deploy-bot: Canary queued: llm-route-mux @ 03:30 UTC. Policy: 0.2% -> 4% (10m soak) -> 20% (manual/auto if metrics OK). Healthcheck cadence 15s. Auto-hold on 3 failed pings or error rate > 0.8%.

nina: ack. Adding release note: "fastfail_route warmup; pinned v3.2-rt; fallback-weight updates". PR #1001 draft ready.

raj: Safety gates proposal: - errorRate > 0.5% sustained for 3m -> hold - p95 delta > +180ms sustained 5m -> hold - sudden p99 spike or DB throttles -> immediate roll back. Also recommend adding a short smoke test run (10 requests) after each ramp step.

ops-anne: Prewarm KV cache for 7m on canary nodes. Set cohort-drain to 40s on rollback. On rollback, run cache-warm on stable fleet to reduce tail. Also suggest tagging deploy metadata: change_window=late-night, owner=kai.

kai: CLI to apply flag for canary (for runbook):
```
infra flag apply fastfail_route --cohort 0.002 --stage smoke --pin model=v3.2-rt --meta "deploy:6333333333;owner=kai"
```

nina: release notes updated in PR #1001 with rollback rules: err>0.5%/p95>+180ms/3 failed pings. Who's oncall?

raj: I'll be primary. ops-anne backup. I'll watch dashboard and run the smoke tests after each ramp.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 6333333350. Health pings active.

kai: first 6m telemetry: errorRate 0.07%, p95 +95ms, p99 +150ms. Running smoke tests post-smoke-stage.

raj: smoke tests passed (10 requests ok). Proceeding to ramp to 4% in 2m.

ops-anne: reminder: keep alert routing set to SMS for this window. If rollback happens, trigger runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/fastfail_route_rollback and set cohort-drain=40s.

nina: I'll post a short customer-facing note after second stage completes.

raj: watching. If any gate trips I'll flip flag to 0 and pin traffic back to stable-v3 route and open an incident thread.

kai: thanks everyone. Keeping this thread for postmortem notes if needed.
